item.title: Fri 20 Nov 16:32 · risk-off · Bitcoin breaks below $60,000 as tech rout deepens
item.description:
60-second briefing:

  1. Bitcoin broke below $60,000 after the US open for the first time since early July, touching about $58,700 on Kraken and trading near $59,200 at 16:30 UK.
  2. The Nasdaq opened 1.2% lower at its lowest since mid-April as Anthropic shares fell to about $87, and the VIX fear gauge rose to 29.5, its highest since March, CoinDesk and Cointelegraph reported.
  3. ZEC fell about 9% since the morning edition to near $775, after a low of about $756; CoinDesk put its 24-hour drop at 11%.

What changed: This morning Bitcoin had stalled near $61,800 and the question was whether the tech selloff would carry into the US session. It did: Bitcoin is about 4% lower than at 06:40 and below $60,000, and ZEC fell more than twice as hard. Next to watch: The US close at 21:00 UK and Friday's ETF flows, due Saturday morning UK. The next 🔴 event is the Fed decision on Wednesday 9 December at 19:00 UK.

Bitcoin breaks below $60,000 as tech rout deepens

The world's largest cryptocurrency fell to about $58,700 in the US session, its lowest since early July, as Anthropic's shares slid and Wall Street volatility jumped.

Bitcoin fell below $60,000 on Friday afternoon for the first time since early July, dropping about $1,800 in roughly an hour after the US open, according to Bitcoin Magazine. Kraken data showed a low of about $58,700 and a price near $59,200 at 16:30 UK time, about 4% below the morning.

The fall came as the Nasdaq Composite opened 1.2% lower at its lowest level since mid-April, Cointelegraph reported. Anthropic shares, which closed their first day at $97.17, fell to about $87, close to their $83 offer price.

More than $700 million of crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours, about 86% of them bets on rising prices, Bitcoin Magazine reported. CoinDesk said Wall Street's VIX volatility index had climbed to 29.5, its highest since March, while a gauge of expected Bitcoin swings rose to 52.

Institutional selling continued in the background. US spot bitcoin ETFs lost $582 million on Thursday, taking November's net outflows to about $3.47 billion, The Block reported from SoSoValue data.

Glassnode said Bitcoin was trading only just above its realised price, the average cost of all coins, Bitcoin Magazine reported. A break below would leave the average holder at a loss for the first time since early 2023. Traders were also pricing a quarter-point Fed rate rise on 9 December, CoinDesk said.

item.title: Fri 20 Nov 06:40 · risk-off · Bitcoin slips to four-month low as ETF selling deepens
item.description:

  2. US spot bitcoin ETFs lost a net $582 million on Thursday, the third straight day of outflows, led by $541 million from BlackRock's IBIT, according to SoSoValue data reported by Bloomingbit.
  3. ZEC fell to about $853, roughly 3.5% below the evening edition, after touching $842 overnight.

What changed: The evening question was whether forced selling below $62,000 would run on overnight. It ran a little further, to about $61,200, then stalled: Bitcoin is slightly above the evening edition. ZEC kept falling, and the first full ETF figure for Thursday confirmed heavy institutional selling. Next to watch: The US open at 14:30 UK and Friday's ETF flows. Bitcoin slips to four-month low as ETF selling deepens

The world's largest cryptocurrency fell to about $61,200 overnight as investors pulled $582 million from US bitcoin funds on Thursday.

Bitcoin fell to about $61,200 on Kraken in the early hours of Friday, its lowest level since early July, before steadying near $61,800 by 06:40 UK time.

The drop followed Thursday's sharp fall on Wall Street after Anthropic's record stock market debut. CoinDesk reported that the AI company's shares opened at $111.50 against an $83 offer price but closed at $97.17, as the Nasdaq fell 2.4%. Nasdaq futures were a further 0.7% lower in Asian hours, CoinDesk said.

Crypto futures worth more than $600 million were liquidated over 24 hours, nearly half of them in the last 12, according to CoinDesk.

US spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds recorded net outflows of $582 million on Thursday, nearly twice Wednesday's figure, according to SoSoValue data reported by Bloomingbit. BlackRock's IBIT accounted for $541 million. It was the third straight day of withdrawals, taking the three-day total to $1.13 billion.

Pressure also showed in Bitcoin-linked shares. Strategy closed down 4.6% at $86.13, its sixth straight fall, Bitcoin Magazine reported, leaving its 850,849 coins about $11 billion below their cost.

Separately, VanEck told Gemini it would end custody of its bitcoin, ether and solana ETFs from about 16 February 2027, CoinDesk reported. Traders now look to the US open at 14:30 UK.

Bitcoin breaks $62,000 as Anthropic debut turns into tech selloff

A blockbuster listing that lifted futures in the morning ended with Wall Street sharply lower and bitcoin at its weakest level since July.

Bitcoin fell below $62,000 on Thursday and traded at about $61,510 on Kraken at 21:30 UK, after touching $61,426. That was about 2% below the afternoon edition and about 2.3% down on the day.

Bitcoin Magazine said the low was the weakest since July and put the fall from 19 October at about 25%. It linked the drop to a broad tech selloff that followed Anthropic's Nasdaq debut, with the Dow down about 1,000 points late in the session.

Anthropic's shares opened at $111.50, 34% above the $83 offer price, CoinDesk reported, briefly valuing the company above $2 trillion. They then traded as low as $95.05, Cointelegraph reported, and were near $97 in late trading. CoinDesk said the Nasdaq, S&P 500 and Dow were each down more than 1.5% in the afternoon.

Crypto-linked shares fell further. Bitcoin Magazine reported Strategy down about 4% and Galaxy Digital down about 6.9%. Decrypt said US spot bitcoin funds had lost about $2.9 billion in November, including $306.4 million on Wednesday.

The fall took bitcoin through the $62,030 area where CoinDesk had earlier placed the largest cluster of leveraged long positions. Thursday's ETF flow figures are due on Friday morning.

Bitcoin fades after US open as Anthropic shares start trading

Bitcoin briefly topped $64,000 as tech futures rallied ahead of Anthropic's Nasdaq debut, then gave the gains back once US trading began.

Fed minutes back more hikes as bitcoin clings to $62,000

Minutes of the Fed's October meeting showed almost all officials expect further rate rises, and bitcoin ended the US session pinned just above its weekend low.

Bitcoin traded at about $62,350 on Kraken at 21:30 UK on Wednesday, down about 3.9% on the day and just above the weekend low near $62,000, after minutes of the Federal Reserve's October meeting pointed to further rate rises.

Almost all participants judged that further increases would likely be appropriate to bring inflation back to 2% in a timely way, according to the minutes released at 19:00 UK. A couple said a rise of more than a quarter point could warrant consideration at the December meeting if inflation data were unfavourable, and many described the AI buildout as a material source of inflation risk. The Fed held rates at 3.75% to 4% in October, with two officials voting for a rise.

The minutes echoed Governor Christopher Waller, who told CNBC on Wednesday that a half-point December rise was probably needed. Analysts quoted by Decrypt also pointed to US spot bitcoin ETF outflows of $239.9 million on Tuesday and a closer link between bitcoin and Nvidia shares.

CryptoQuant said bitcoin had slipped back into a bearish phase below its 200-day average near $72,900, The Block reported, though it flagged $62,000 to $65,000 as a 'value zone'.

Separately, Binance said an Abu Dhabi court had granted a $6.5 billion worldwide freezing order over its October hack. Anthropic's shares are due to start trading on Nasdaq on Thursday.
